purpose: Seven independent room concepts and a faction prop/equipment panel. Exact artificial coordinates remain in B02.json and the separately rendered layout maps.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: A single polished game level concept board for B02 Amber Hive, a bright fantasy action RPG.
Input image 1 is ONLY a rendering style reference: inherit its warm sunlight, bright painterly cartoon fantasy, clean ink edges, 2.5D volume, three-quarter high-angle near-isometric camera, consistent actor scale and clear floor. Do not copy its machines, winches, architecture, HUD, text or exact composition.
Create a very high-resolution landscape board, ideally 3840 x 2160. EXACTLY 4 columns by 2 rows, with eight equally sized, clearly separated panels and narrow cream gutters. The first SEVEN panels each contain a COMPLETE DISTINCT INDEPENDENT playable room, never a cropped segment of a large connected map. Panel eight is a detailed prop and equipment collection. A restrained cream-and-brass board edge can echo the reference parchment UI.
Only seven small dark-purple panel labels, verbatim: row 1 "L07", "L08", "L09", "L10"; row 2 "L11", "L12", "BO02"; no text in the eighth panel. No other text. No HUD, icons overlaid on scenes, arrows or coordinate diagram.
Unified world: a living insect civilization built by bees, beetles, mantises, dragonflies and glowworms. Open sunlit honey-valley terraces with warm pale amber continuous ground, translucent resin details, cream beeswax, light green giant leaves, vivid violet wing membranes, emerald insect eyes. Wonder and playful fantasy inventions. Rich varied perimeter props: leaf sailing boats, beeswax market stalls, dew-shell dishes, butterfly wind chimes, translucent cocoons, wing banners, leaf looms, glowing amber lanterns, colorful empty shell sculptures, pollen flowers, flower-shaped treasure coffers. At least three visually distinct insect enemies in each combat panel with readable colorful segmented silhouettes.
Each scene is designed by hand, with a large unobstructed center and a readable broad winding ground route. Most props frame the room perimeter. Show small crystal-flower beacon fixtures, two or three egg-nest objectives and one side-path flower treasure coffer in each room. The exact numerical placement is in separate layout diagrams; this board should faithfully communicate the seven themes, landmark locations and open route character.
Panel L07: Honey-crystal ferry. A beeswax spice market at upper left and a fantastical giant-leaf honey pier with a violet-wing leaf sailboat along lower-right edge. Main open route arrives lower left, crosses the broad middle, bends to the upper-right exit. Two small egg nests. The pier is peripheral, not a huge pool or split floor.
Panel L08: Wing watch terrace. A central-upper insect observatory pavilion with violet wing-membrane canopy and a dragonfly compound-eye lens; suspended floating insect nests visible only beyond the top outer edge. Broad continuous main route forms a lower arc from left to right. Upper side path leads to the observatory and flower coffer. Three small egg nests.
Panel L09: Molting ceremony garden. Upper-edge translucent empty beetle shells displayed on low cream beeswax plinths with leafy rite crowns; colorful cocoon racks and baby leaf cradles. A spacious main path sweeps diagonally from upper left to lower right through an open courtyard. Three egg nests; flower coffer upper right. No dense maze walls.
Panel L10: Pollen ventilation well. A giant flower-stamen windwell at the upper-center edge, surrounded by organic green-and-violet wind petals and narrow translucent resin veins. No industrial fans. Wide route rises diagonally from lower left to center upper and exits mid-right. Two egg nests. Flower coffer upper right.
Panel L11: Leafweavers' sunlit cavern forecourt. A leafy mantis-arm loom with dew-drop shuttles and violet silk at the lower-center edge. A bright scalloped insect grotto and empty chitin-shell arch ONLY beyond the top perimeter. Main route uses a wide northern arc before reaching the right exit; lower-left side path leads to the research coffer. Three egg nests.
Panel L12: Honeyflow garden gate. A huge flower-calyx gate with translucent honey veins at the upper-right outer edge. Narrow branching resin channels confined to the perimeter, and a broad COMPLETE DRY CENTRAL GARDEN. Broad lower arc main route, left-lower flower coffer and three small egg nests. Do not place a water pool in the room.
Panel BO02: Queen's sunny nursery. South entrance, north exit, large oval clear battle court, ornate four-petal beeswax nursery crown throne along top edge. Paint a real huge AMBER INSECT QUEEN standing in the upper middle, front of the throne: six elegant segmented legs, amber-gold thorax, emerald egg sac, translucent violet wings, a flower crown, huge but charming insect anatomy, not humanoid princess. Three guarded egg nests west, north, east. Tiny mantis and larva attendants. Three small crystal-flower beacons at western/southwestern/eastern margins. Pale thin readable preview shapes for a few circular amber acid landing zones, a directional wing fan, and glowing threads to the egg nests, not big opaque warning overlays.
Panel eight: crisp separate close-ups of the unique insect props, a wing-membrane weapon, a chitin-acid weapon, queen flower-crown helmet and emerald egg-sac talisman; show volume, exquisite hand-painted material and imaginative anatomy-derived mechanisms. No numbered labels.
Lighting: bright warm afternoon sun from upper left, violet cast shadows, creamy bounced light; fresh lively colors, painterly detail with low visual noise on playable ground.
Avoid: grey darkness, gore or rotten bodies, industrial winches, steel cables, machine coils, generic mineral crates, giant rectangular water holes, stretches of texture masquerading as a wall, giant blocking terrain slabs, narrow corridors, stretched sprites, clutter on the main combat ground, flat vector diagrams, photorealism, a single room repeated seven times, a large map sliced into panels, watermark.
Perimeter requirement: in every independent room, render finished natural edges, not a rectangular tilemap clipped into grey empty space. Warm ground transitions through small wax/stone fragments, pollen flowers and leaves, then gently curving low beeswax terrace rims, visible leaf-root bases and complete sunlit amber hive-valley backdrop. Each room uses its own inhabited perimeter landmark. Extend entrance and exit ground under leafy gate canopies. Tiny soft-focus leaves only at bottom corners; never obscure the main ground, heroine-sized actors or warning shapes. No grey border or grey void.
